source.title: Report on Resource Adequacy Plan for Kerala (Up to 2035-36), Version 2.0
source.caveat: This is an official planning study and validation reference. Contracted capacity, forecast requirement and the CEA study's demand accounting are kept separate from Kerala Economic Review installed-capacity and sales definitions.

actual_2024_25.note: These actual values use CEA resource-adequacy accounting. The peak differs from the Kerala Economic Review/KSEBL maximum peak reference of 5797 MW, so neither value is silently substituted for the other.

hourly_demand_2024_25.seasonal_note: Demand is higher from February to May.
hourly_demand_2024_25.april_pattern_note: Two peaks are visible, approximately daytime 15:00 and night 23:00.
hourly_demand_2024_25.rule: Any reconstructed hourly chronology must remain labelled proxy/reconstruction until the underlying Kerala SLDC/KSEBL hourly or 15-minute telemetry is obtained.

contracted_capacity_march_2025_mw.scope_note: Contracted capacity, not in-state installed capacity.

likely_optimal_contracted_capacity_2035_.note: CEA study result retained as an external planning benchmark, not adopted as the Kerala 2040 model optimum.
